proposals.before: Book of Sui, 56th year of Volume, 21th year of Biography
proposals.after: Book of Sui, Volume 56, Biography 21
proposals.reason: The heading names Volume 56, Biography 21; 卷 and 列傳 are not 'years'.

proposals.before: Before this, envoys had often followed Chen court etiquette. When Kai led the mission, he adhered entirely to Sui protocol, and the Chen side could not make him yield.
proposals.after: Before this, envoys had often followed Chen court etiquette. When Kai led the mission, he adhered entirely to his own court's protocol, and the Chen side could not make him yield.
proposals.reason: 本朝 in this still-Zhou embassy scene is Kai's own court, not Sui.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he was given the additional title Pillar of State, Third Rank, dismissed as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, advanced in rank to Marquis, and still acted as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Kaihuang, he was given the additional title Pillar of State, Third Rank, appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, advanced in rank to Marquis, and still acted as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 除 in appointment formulae means to appoint, not to dismiss.

proposals.before: The prosecutors reported: "Fang Gongyi was a partisan of Yuwen Jiong and should never have been promoted.
proposals.after: The prosecutors reported: "Fang Gongyi was a partisan of Yuchi Jiong and should never have been promoted.
proposals.reason: Chinese 尉遲迥 is Yuchi Jiong, not a Yuwen.

proposals.before: Since Zhou times official selection had made no distinction between worthy and unworthy. When Kai took charge of personnel, he worked with Xue Daoheng and Lu Yanshi to sort the gentry by merit, and thus provoked the slander of She Danggu—which brought him to this end.
proposals.after: Since Zhou times official selection had made no distinction between worthy and unworthy. When Kai took charge of personnel, he worked with Xue Daoheng and Lu Yanshi to sort the gentry by merit, and thus incurred the slander of forming a solid clique—which brought him to this end.
proposals.reason: 故涉黨固之譖 is 'thereby became involved in slander of factional solidarity', not a person named She Danggu.

proposals.before: From the Zhou dynasty onward selection had no distinction of pure and impure; when Kai acted in the Ministry of Personnel, he with Xue Daoheng, Lu Yanshi, and others discriminated among the gentry streams, and so he fell under the slanders of the faction of She Danggu.
proposals.after: From the Zhou dynasty onward selection had no distinction of pure and impure; when Kai acted in the Ministry of Personnel, he with Xue Daoheng, Lu Yanshi, and others discriminated among the gentry streams, and so he fell under slanders of clique-forming.
proposals.reason: 黨固之譖 is slander about factional rigidity, not a named She Danggu.

proposals.before: At the battle of Heyin an edict ordered him to serve while still in mourning garb. On his return he was appointed senior clerk in the bureau of appointments, inherited the title Duke of Pengyang, and received a fief of twenty-one hundred households.
proposals.after: At the battle of Heyin an edict ordered him to serve while still in mourning garb. On his return he was appointed junior grand master of the Bureau of Operations, inherited the title Duke of Pengyang, and received a fief of twenty-one hundred households.
proposals.reason: 職方下大夫 is Zhifang (operations), not the bureau of appointments.

proposals.before: In the campaign at Heyin, an edict ordered him to serve in ink-stained mourning garb; on return he was appointed Senior Clerk in the Bureau of Appointments, inherited the rank of Duke of Pengyang County, with a fief of 2,100 households.
proposals.after: In the campaign at Heyin, an edict ordered him to serve in ink-stained mourning garb; on return he was appointed Junior Grand Master of the Bureau of Operations, inherited the rank of Duke of Pengyang County, with a fief of 2,100 households.
proposals.reason: Literal field repeats the 職方 mistranslation as appointments.

proposals.before: When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, Xi served in his existing post as acting chief censor.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, Xi served in his existing post as acting Neiyan.
proposals.reason: 納言 is the inner-court spokesman, not the censorate.

proposals.before: At the moment Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Xi acted in the duties of Chief Censor in his original post.
proposals.after: At the moment Emperor Gaozu received the abdication, Xi acted in the duties of Neiyan in his original post.
proposals.reason: Literal field repeats the 納言 office error.

proposals.before: He ordered Dou Lutong, governor of Xiangzhou, to adopt Xi's methods.
proposals.after: He ordered Doulu Tong, governor of Xiangzhou, to adopt Xi's methods.
proposals.reason: 豆盧 is the compound surname Doulu, not Dou plus Lutong.

proposals.before: He ordered Governor of Xiangzhou Dou Lutong to study Xi's methods.
proposals.after: He ordered Governor of Xiangzhou Doulu Tong to study Xi's methods.
proposals.reason: Same compound-surname error for 豆盧通 in the literal field.

proposals.before: He rose repeatedly to pillar of state, was soon appointed senior clerk in the bureau of metals, and later received the additional rank of pillar of state.
proposals.after: He rose repeatedly to Shang Yitong, was soon appointed daifu of the Bureau of Metals, and later received the additional rank of kaifu.
proposals.reason: 上儀同 and 開府 are distinct honorific offices; neither is 柱國, yet the idiomatic version renders both as pillar of state.

proposals.before: He was summoned as grand master for imperial entertainments, soon transferred to grand master for law. He applied the law with breadth and fairness and was regarded as competent in office.
proposals.after: He was summoned as Chamberlain of the Palace Guards, soon transferred to Chamberlain for Law Enforcement. He applied the law with breadth and fairness and was regarded as competent in office.
proposals.reason: 衛尉卿 is the palace-guards chamberlain, not grand master for imperial entertainments; 大理卿 is the chief judicial chamberlain.

proposals.before: Governor Shangguan Zheng requested aid from Zhou. Zhou feared Liang's military edge and did not dare refuse. Liang then led troops to attack Zhou. Zhou wished to repel him by stratagem and sent his close associate Lu Shifan to tell Liang, "Affairs under Heaven are not yet settled. Zhou, as a minister, must choose his stand according to what is fitting. Why rush to attack one another?"
proposals.after: Governor Shangguan Zheng requested aid from Zhou. Zhou feared Prince Liang's military edge and did not dare resist. Qi Liang then led troops to attack Zhou. Zhou wished to repel him by stratagem and sent his close associate Lu Shifan to tell Qi Liang, "Affairs under Heaven are not yet settled. Zhou, as a minister, must choose his stand according to what is fitting. Why rush to attack one another?"
proposals.reason: Chinese contrasts 諒 (Prince Liang) with 良 (Qi Liang); the idiomatic English renders both as Liang, and 不敢拒 means he did not dare resist.

proposals.before: He had sons named He and Xian, both of whom became well known.
proposals.after: He had sons named Zi and Xian, both of whom became well known.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names are 子 and 獻; He does not match 子.

proposals.before: Later he followed the emperor in pacifying Qi. For his merit he was appointed pillar of state, enfeoffed as duke of Wuwei county with a fief of fifteen hundred households, granted fifteen hundred bolts of goods, a hundred fifty slaves and maidservants, and more than a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, and was made registrar to the governor-general of Si prefecture.
proposals.after: Later he followed the emperor in pacifying Qi. For his merit he was appointed Senior Yitong, enfeoffed as duke of Wuwei county with a fief of fifteen hundred households, granted fifteen hundred bolts of goods, a hundred fifty slaves and maidservants, and more than a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, and was made registrar to the governor-general of Si prefecture.
proposals.reason: 上儀同 is the honorific rank Shang Yitong, not the separate title 柱國 (pillar of state).

proposals.before: Later he followed the Emperor in pacifying Qi; for merit he was appointed Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuwei County with a fief of 1,500 households, granted 1,500 bolts of goods, 150 slaves and maidservants, and over a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, and appointed Registrar to the Governor-General of Si Prefecture.
proposals.after: Later he followed the Emperor in pacifying Qi; for merit he was appointed Senior Yitong, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuwei County with a fief of 1,500 households, granted 1,500 bolts of goods, 150 slaves and maidservants, and over a thousand horses, cattle, and sheep, and appointed Registrar to the Governor-General of Si Prefecture.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 上儀同 as Pillar of State, which is a different Zhou-Sui rank.

proposals.before: He was appointed governor of Huai prefecture and soon transferred to governor of South Si prefecture.
proposals.after: He was appointed governor of Kuai prefecture and soon transferred to governor of South Si prefecture.
proposals.reason: 澮州 is Kuai/Hui prefecture (澮), not Huai (淮).

proposals.before: He was appointed Governor of Huai Prefecture and soon transferred to Governor of South Si Prefecture.
proposals.after: He was appointed Governor of Kuai Prefecture and soon transferred to Governor of South Si Prefecture.
proposals.reason: The same Huai/澮 confusion appears in the literal English.

proposals.before: He received the additional rank pillar of state, was promoted to minister of punishments, and led the crown prince's guard of honored attendants.
proposals.after: He received the additional rank of Kaifu, was promoted to minister of punishments, and led the crown prince's guard of honored attendants.
proposals.reason: 加開府 is the Kaifu honor, not 柱國 pillar of state.

proposals.before: He was given the additional rank Pillar of State, promoted and appointed Minister of Punishments, and led the Crown Prince's Guard of Honored Attendants.
proposals.after: He was given the additional rank of Kaifu, promoted and appointed Minister of Punishments, and led the Crown Prince's Guard of Honored Attendants.
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats the pillar-of-state mistranslation of 開府.

proposals.before: At that time the emperor gradually favored music and women and was especially zealous in distant campaigns. Bi said to Gao Jiong, "In the past Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou favored music and women and the state perished. Compared with today, is it not even worse?"
proposals.after: At that time the emperor gradually favored music and women and was especially zealous in distant campaigns. Bi said to Gao Jiong, "In the past the Tianyuan Emperor of Zhou favored music and women and the state perished. Compared with today, is it not even worse?"
proposals.reason: 周天元 is Zhou's Tianyuan Emperor (Emperor Xuan, Yuwen Yun), not Emperor Wu (武帝).

proposals.before: At that time the Emperor gradually favored music and women and was especially zealous in distant campaigns; Bi said to Gao Jiong: "In the past Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou favored music and women and the state perished—compared with today, is it not even more so?"
proposals.after: At that time the Emperor gradually favored music and women and was especially zealous in distant campaigns; Bi said to Gao Jiong: "In the past the Tianyuan Emperor of Zhou favored music and women and the state perished—compared with today, is it not even more so?"
proposals.reason: The literal field likewise identifies 天元 as Emperor Wu.

proposals.before: He was appointed pillar of state, granted a hundred thirty slaves and maidservants, five hundred bolts of goods, and gold, silver, and mixed livestock in full measure.
proposals.after: He was appointed kaifu, granted a hundred thirty slaves and maidservants, five hundred bolts of goods, and gold, silver, and mixed livestock in full measure.
proposals.reason: 開府 is kaifu rank (authority to establish an office), not 柱國 'pillar of state'.

proposals.before: He was appointed Pillar of State, granted 130 slaves and maidservants, 500 bolts of goods, and gold, silver, and mixed livestock in full measure.
proposals.after: He was appointed Kaifu, granted 130 slaves and maidservants, 500 bolts of goods, and gold, silver, and mixed livestock in full measure.
proposals.reason: 開府 is kaifu rank, not 'Pillar of State'.

proposals.before: Minister of rites Yang Xuangan's envoy arrived at Jiangdu. That man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.
proposals.after: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan arrived on a mission at Jiangdu. That man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.
proposals.reason: 楊玄感使至江都 uses 使 as the mission verb: Yang Xuangan himself arrived at Jiangdu; the English invents a separate envoy.

proposals.before: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan's envoy arrived at Jiangdu; that man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.
proposals.after: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan arrived on a mission at Jiangdu; that man went to Xuangan to proclaim his grievance.
proposals.reason: Same 使至 construction: Yang Xuangan came on mission, not 'Yang Xuangan's envoy'.

proposals.before: His father Chen held the rank pillar of state, third rank. When Wang became honored, Chen was posthumously granted duke of Pingxiang county.
proposals.after: His father Chen held the rank Equal to the Three Excellencies. When Wang became honored, Chen was posthumously granted duke of Pingxiang county.
proposals.reason: 儀同三司 is Equal to the Three Excellencies, not the separate rank pillar of the state.

proposals.before: His father Chen was Pillar of State, Third Rank; when Wang became honored, he was posthumously granted Duke of Pingxiang County.
proposals.after: His father Chen was Equal to the Three Excellencies; when Wang became honored, he was posthumously granted Duke of Pingxiang County.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 儀同三司 as Pillar of State, Third Rank.

proposals.before: When Emperor Gaozu was at Xiang, he was summoned to advise on military affairs and transferred to grand master for the court below.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gaozu was Counsellor-in-chief, he was summoned to advise on military affairs and transferred to grand master for the court below.
proposals.reason: 居相 means occupying the chancellorship, not residence at a place named Xiang.

proposals.before: When Emperor Gaozu was at Xiang, he was summoned to know military affairs and transferred to Grand Master for the Court Below.
proposals.after: When Emperor Gaozu occupied the chancellorship, he was summoned to know military affairs and transferred to Grand Master for the Court Below.
proposals.reason: The same misreading of 居相 as a toponym appears in the literal line.

proposals.before: Da thereupon spoke privately to Wang: "I shall recommend you as left vice director. If the matter succeeds, I shall repay you with good fields."
proposals.after: Da thereupon spoke privately to Wang: "I shall recommend you as left vice director. If the matter succeeds, you should repay me with good fields."
proposals.reason: The punishment of Da shows 相報 is a requested bribe from Wang, not Da giving fields.

proposals.before: Da thereupon spoke privately to Wang: "I shall recommend you as Left Vice Director; if the matter succeeds, I should repay you with good fields."
proposals.after: Da thereupon spoke privately to Wang: "I shall recommend you as Left Vice Director; if the matter succeeds, you should repay me with good fields."
proposals.reason: Literal English reverses the silent subject of 當以良田相報.

proposals.before: When Emperor Yang died, Wang Shichong installed Prince Tong of Yue as ruler and summoned Wang as minister of personnel. He was greatly trusted and relied upon.
proposals.after: When Emperor Yang died, Wang Shichong installed Tong, Prince of Yue, as ruler and summoned Wang as minister of personnel. He was greatly trusted and relied upon.
proposals.reason: 越王侗 is Tong, Prince of Yue, not Prince Tong of Yue as if Tong were the fief.

s0062 職方下大夫 is junior grand master of Zhifang (operations), not a senior clerk of appointments.
s0062 職方下大夫 is the Bureau of Operations junior grand master; appointments is a mistranslation of 職方.
s0065 以本官行納言事 is acting nayan, the inner-court spokesman, not chief censor.

Zhou wished to repel him by stratagem and sent his close associate Lu Shifan to tell Qi Liang, "Affairs under Heaven are not yet settled. Zhou, as a minister, must choose his stand according to what is fitting. Why rush to attack one another?"

s0172 上儀同 is Senior Yitong; rendering it Pillar of State conflates two Zhou-Sui ranks.

s0227 開府 is kaifu rank, not Pillar of State.

s0266 儀同三司 is Equal to the Three Excellencies, not pillar of state.
s0266 儀同三司 is Equal to the Three Excellencies, not Pillar of State, Third Rank.

s0272 居相 is occupying the chancellorship, not a toponym Xiang.

decisions.reason: s0278 the silent subject of 當以良田相報 is Wang repaying Da, not Da giving fields.
